You have attempted this same task before and did not succeed. These are the plans you wrote after those attempts.
Trial #1: New plan: I failed because I repeatedly moved back and forth between the same rooms (Library, Sauna, Wine cellar) without checking if I had already visited them, causing an infinite loop instead of exploring new areas. I did not maintain a mental list of visited rooms to track my progress. Next time, I will first list all currently visited rooms in my graph before making a move. When presented with a direction, I will check if the destination room is already in my visited list; if it is, I will immediately choose a different untried direction or stop if no new directions exist. I will only move to a new room if it is not yet in my graph's nodes, ensuring I never re-enter a known room unless necessary to reach an unvisited one, and I will declare "DONE" only when all reachable rooms are in my graph.

Trial #2: New plan: I failed because I entered a loop between the Wine cellar, Exercise room, and Foyer, repeatedly choosing directions that led back to already visited nodes instead of exploring new ones. I did not proactively check the list of visited rooms before selecting a direction. Next time, I will first identify all currently visited rooms from my graph. When presented with available directions, I will check if the destination of each direction is already in the visited list. If a direction leads to a known room, I will immediately discard it and select an untried direction that leads to a new room. I will only declare "DONE" after confirming that all reachable directions lead to rooms already present in my graph's nodes.
